terms.gloss: bead; anything round like a berry
terms.register: vōx dē margarītīs plērumque poētica: Hor., Ov.
evidence: Verg. A. 1.655: monīle bācātum, a pearl necklace
terms.comment: The berry word, in the house spelling, used of pearls and, in Prudentius, of the berry-shaped links of a chain (Lewis & Short); so the nearest classical word for a bead. Context tells it from a berry.

evidence: M-O s.v. rosary, after Du Cange: sacrōrum globulōrum seriēs
terms.comment: The bead of a rosary in later Latin; classically a little ball (Plin.). In the lexicon also the button.

evidence: M-O s.v. rosary, after Erasmus: sphaerulae precātōriae
terms.comment: Late Latin for a small ball; Erasmus’s word for the beads of a rosary.

phrases.english: Let’s thread the beads on a string.

sources: Lewis & Short: baca · Lewis & Short: bacatus · Lewis & Short: globulus · Lewis & Short: sphaerula · Lewis & Short: linum
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. objects: rosary (beads). Traupman has only the pearl necklace, monīle baccātum (pp. 115, 117); Levi–Bini has no word.
